description: A/B the single-CTA-panel<512> + UNIFORM-TF32-trailing lever (which won n=1024 by 1.44-1.60x by dropping the per-matrix classify/argsort/gather reorder) against the cooperative CLUSTER panel currently used for n=2048 B=8 and n=4096 B=2. The cluster was chosen for these work-starved shapes, but a sibling showed at n=1024 that the per-matrix reorder overhead + threads=128 cost MORE than the cluster's benefit — the win was single-CTA panel at threads=512 + uniform TF32. Test whether the SAME simpler lever beats the cluster at n=2048/4096: route n=2048 and n=4096 to the single-CTA blocked panel at threads=512 (or swept) with uniform TF32 trailing (budget loose: ~5e-3 at 2048, ~1e-2 at 4096, so uniform TF32 safe for ALL conditioning there) instead of _blocked_qr_cluster. If the cluster's per-column cluster.sync overhead exceeds its occupancy benefit even at B=8/B=2 (as it did at B=60), the simpler path wins. Back-to-back A/B vs the cluster (current n=2048 ~15k, n=4096 ~31k clean) + nsys total-GPU-time. Keep n!=2048/4096 as parent. FP32 panel; no 'stream' substring.

Trial 1: route n=2048/4096 to SINGLE-CTA _blocked_qr (threads=512) + uniform TF32, dropping the cooperative cluster. n=2048 cb=16; n=4096 cb=12 (single-CTA cb=16 is 262KB>232KB B200 cap -- the cluster's per-CTA m/K row-split is why only it affords cb=16 at n=4096). All 22 tests+3 guards CLEAN; n=2048 rankdef scaled_factor_residual=3.45, n=4096 dense=0.416, upper=0 -- uniform TF32 numerically safe at both. CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve A/B (both captured 2.0 solve-batches, median-per-launch x launches): n=2048 single-CTA 15847us vs cluster 13781us = single 1.15x SLOWER; n=4096 single-CTA 48861us vs cluster 28554us = single 1.71x SLOWER. CONFIRMS the cluster is right for these work-starved low-batch shapes (B=8/B=2 -> single-CTA uses only 8/2 SMs of 148; cluster K=8/K=16 fills them). Heavy-contention benchmark geomean 12419us (parent same window ~13230us; both ~1.6x inflated).

Trial 4 (FINAL = best single-CTA config): n=2048 cb=16, n=4096 cb=12, both threads=512, uniform TF32, NO cluster. All 22 tests+3 guards CLEAN. CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve-batch VERDICT across the full sweep: n=2048 single-CTA(cb16/512)=15847us vs cluster=13781us (cluster 1.15x faster); n=4096 single-CTA(cb12/512)=48861us vs cluster=28554us (cluster 1.71x faster). Sweep showed threads 512>256 both shapes; n=2048 cb 16>24 (panel serial work ~cb^2). CONFIRMS the cluster is right for these work-starved low-batch shapes -- the n=1024 B=60 lever does NOT transfer to B=8/B=2 where single-CTA uses only 8/2 of 148 SMs. Heavy-contention benchmark geomean 12423us (shape5 n=2048 54402us, shape6 n=4096 168810us -- benchmark per-shape too contention-noisy to rank, hence nsys).

Trial 2: single-CTA threads SWEEP -> 256 (vs 512). n=2048 cb=16, n=4096 cb=12, uniform TF32, NO cluster. All 22 tests+3 guards CLEAN. CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve-batch: n=2048 threads256=16250us vs threads512=15847us (512 faster); n=4096 threads256=52893us vs threads512=48861us (512 faster). Both LOSE to cluster (n=2048 13781us, n=4096 28554us). Confirms 512 is the better single-CTA width (tall panels need more warps to hide per-column reduction latency). Benchmark measured in a LOW-contention window: geomean 8732us (shape5 n=2048 38191us, shape6 n=4096 122205us).

Trial 3: widen n=2048 single-CTA panel to cb=24 (vs 16), threads=512; n=4096 cb=12/512. Tests whether fewer-but-fatter panels (128->86 at n=2048) narrow the single-CTA gap to the cluster. All 22 tests+3 guards CLEAN; n=2048 rankdef scaled_factor_residual=3.45 (uniform TF32 stable at cb=24). CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve-batch: n=2048 cb=24=16766us vs cb=16=15847us -> cb=24 WORSE (2-level panel serial work ~cb^2, so the fatter panel's per-launch cost 161us > 2x cb=16's 89us). Still LOSES to cluster (13781us). cb=16 is the best single-CTA width at n=2048. Benchmark (heavy contention) geomean 12423us (shape5 n=2048 54241us).

Brief 40 A/B COMPLETE: the n=1024 winning lever (single-CTA panel threads=512 + uniform TF32, NO cluster/reorder) does NOT transfer to the work-starved n=2048 B=8 / n=4096 B=2 shapes -- the cooperative CLUSTER wins both. This VALIDATES the parent's current cluster routing for n=2048/4096.

CONTENTION-IMMUNE VERDICT (nsys per-solve-batch = sum(median-per-launch x launches/solve); the heavy ~4x fleet contention made raw benchmark per-shape useless and even SIGN-FLIPPED n=2048, so nsys is authoritative; reproduced identically on trial 1 AND trial 4):
  n=2048: best single-CTA(cb16/threads512)=15.8ms vs cluster=13.8ms  -> cluster 1.15x faster
  n=4096: best single-CTA(cb12/threads512)=48.7ms vs cluster=28.6ms  -> cluster 1.71x faster

SWEEPS done within the brief (all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN every trial; uniform TF32 numerically safe at both n -- n=2048 rankdef scaled_factor_residual=3.45, n=4096 dense=0.416, upper=0):
  - threads {256,512}: 512 wins BOTH shapes (tall panels need more warps to hide per-column reduction latency: n=2048 256=16.3ms>512=15.8ms; n=4096 256=52.9ms>512=48.7ms).
  - n=2048 cb {16,24}: 16 wins (the 2-level panel's serial work scales ~cb^2, so the fatter cb=24 panel's per-launch cost 161us > 2x cb=16's 89us; cb=24=16.8ms>cb=16=15.8ms).

WHY the cluster wins here but LOST at n=1024 B=60: at B=8/B=2 the single-CTA panel runs only 8/2 CTAs on 148 SMs (1.3-5% occupancy) -- the cluster's K=8/K=16 row-split gives 64/32 co-resident CTAs and its per-column cluster.sync overhead does NOT exceed that occupancy gain at this low batch. At n=1024 B=60, 60 CTAs already gave the single-CTA panel decent occupancy, so there the cluster.sync overhead dominated. A HARD SMEM wall compounds n=4096: single-CTA holds the whole (m+1)*cb panel in ONE CTA (cb=16 at n=4096 = 262KB > 232KB B200 cap), forcing cb<=12 -> 342 panels vs the cluster's cb=16/241 panels (the cluster splits m across K CTAs so each holds only m/K rows). That extra-panel/extra-GEMM tax is why n=4096's gap (1.71x) is far worse than n=2048's (1.15x).

Final HEAD 432a5473 = the strongest single-CTA config measured (cb16/threads512 at n=2048, cb12/threads512 at n=4096), so the branch tip captures the best version of the explored idea. n!=2048/4096 byte-identical to parent. Profiles for trial 1, trial 2 (256), trial 3 (cb24), and final trial 4 saved under brief-40-trial-*-n{2048,4096}-*.nsys-{rep,txt}.

OPEN DIRECTIONS for the manager (this brief closes single-CTA-replaces-cluster as a loss, but adjacent levers on the CLUSTER path are untried here): (1) sweep the cluster's K and mhyb on the CURRENT faster panel base (parent uses K=8/n=2048, K=16/n=4096, mhyb=256 -- the K=8 was swept on an OLDER base per the code comments; a fresh K sweep at n=2048 B=8 and revisiting mhyb could squeeze the cluster further); (2) the cluster's short-trailing-panel handoff currently uses single-CTA threads=512 -- could the crossover mhyb go lower/higher; (3) cluster panel cb sweep at n=2048 (code says cb=16 is the n=4096 optimum from brief 13 but n=2048 cluster cb was inherited, not re-swept on this base); (4) a HYBRID where n=2048 uses the cluster ONLY for the tallest few panels then single-CTA earlier. None of these are single-CTA-vs-cluster (this brief's question); they tune the cluster that won.
